title: Greenline POC Security Brief & Workshop Notes
content:
Purpose: Draft security brief and workshop capture for Greenline (Greenline HealthTech) POC. This doc bundles the security posture summary we presented during the Sept 30 workshop, the live-action checklist for the POC, and a prioritized evidence list for their InfoSec team. Intended audience: SEs, Security/Compliance reviewers, Greenline security leads.

Executive summary: Greenline asked for a short, runnable POC to evaluate Redwood Private (VPC-deployed control plane + dedicated inference) for processing de-identified PHI-like records. Primary concerns raised: network isolation, encryption key custody, logging/audit retention, and formal proof points for SOC2/ISO mapping. We recommended a dedicated Private deployment in their Azure tenant (customer-managed VNet) with explicit KMS integration, strict CIDR egress rules, and tokenized logging.

Workshop notes (2025-09-30):
- 09:00 – 09:15 Intro / goals (Greenline: reduce latency for batch inference, preserve auditability)
- 09:15 – 10:00 Threat model walkthrough (SE-led). Key decisions: no public egress from inference nodes, control-plane API access limited to management bastion + corporate SSO.
- 10:00 – 10:30 Evidence mapping review: Greenline requested artifacts that prove config and runtime controls; we agreed to provide runbooks plus redacted logs.
- 10:30 – 11:00 Action items & owners assigned.

High-level control summary provided to Greenline: 
- Network controls: VNet peering, NSG rules, private endpoints only for control-plane; restrict inference node egress to customer-approved outbound IPs.
- AuthN/AuthZ: OIDC integration with Greenline Okta tenant; role-mapped RBAC for operations; short-lived credentials for runtime.
- Key management: Customer-managed keys (Azure Key Vault). We will provide an encrypted secrets manifest and a key rotation runbook.
- Data protection: In-transit TLS1.3 enforced; at-rest AES-256 using customer CMK. Temporary KV cache stored on ephemeral instance storage and wiped on termination.
- Observability: Structured audit logs, request/response hashes (non-PII), and per-request trace ID. Logs delivered to customer SIEM via private connector (TLS over private link).
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 control mapping, configuration snapshots, test evidences (screenshot + timestamped command outputs).

Evidence list to deliver (priority order):
1) Network diagram (annotated) showing Private deployment and peering — attach diagram and export (PNG + source).
2) Example NSG and route table export (redacted) — commands and resulting JSON.
3) Okta OIDC configuration screenshots and SSO test trace (success/fail).
4) KMS key policy (customer CMK) and sample enveloping log demonstrating use of CMK for model weights + token encryption.
5) Audit log extract (last 7 days) with redaction plan and mapping to GDPR/PHI minimization notes.
6) Pod/instance termination script output showing disk scrubbing on shutdown.
7) Simple load test run showing baseline latency under dedicated pool with telemetry dump.
8) Pen test summary (third-party vendor scoping doc and planned start date).

Working-runbook snippets we promised during the session (to include in evidence bundle):
- KMS bind: steps for granting Redwood runtime the Key Encrypt/Decrypt role within customer Key Vault (+ sample Azure CLI).
- Private connector: steps to create private endpoint and route table entries, plus sample tcpdump command to verify no internet egress.
- Audit pull: Azure Monitor query examples to pull activity logs filtered by resource tags and trace id.
- Log redaction: sed/grep recipe used to redact sensitive fields before sending examples to Greenline.

Open questions (need SE/security input before sending):
- Greenline asked whether model artifacts can be hashed and verified externally — need to confirm hash strategy for quantized artifacts. (Owner: Ethan Rivera, JIRA-SE-3453)
- Retention policy: Greenline requires 7 years for some audit items; need legal confirmation that Redwood can retain audit metadata that long in Private deployments. (Owner: Priya Patel)
- Pen-test scope: Greenline wants to include UI layer; confirm whether UI will be customer-managed or within the Redwood control plane for the POC.

Risks / Mitigations discussed: 
- Risk: accidental leak during evidence bundle redaction. Mitigation: automate redaction step + second reviewer sign-off before transmission; provide checksum and sample redaction log.
- Risk: SSO misconfiguration causing elevated access. Mitigation: supply test accounts and preflight checklist; run a controlled failover (canary) for RBAC changes.

Deliverable schedule (agreed):
- 2025-10-03: Draft evidence bundle (initial) delivered to Greenline security distribution list.
- 2025-10-10: Finalized runbooks and scripted exports (after internal review).
- 2025-10-17: Optional joint walkthrough with Greenline for evidence verification and KMS binding test.

Assigned owners (quick list):
- Evidence bundle assembly + redaction: Maya Chen
- Network diagrams + NSG exports: James Okafor
- KMS/runbook scripting: Ethan Rivera
- Legal/retention consult: Priya Patel

Attachments to produce (filenames to appear in bundle):
- greenline_network_diagram_2025-09-30.png
- nsgroutes_export_greenline.json.redacted.txt
- okta_oidc_config_screenshot_0910.png
- kms_policy_envelope_example.txt
- audit_extract_sample_redacted.log
- disk_wipe_demo_2025-09-29.txt
- loadtest_baseline_1000rps.csv

Communication notes for sending: Use encrypted email to Greenline sec distribution list, include checksum for each artifact, and add a short statement of redaction methodology. Create Confluence evidence page (CONF-553) and link to bundle. Patch JIRA-SE-3421 with links to artifacts and mark for closure after Greenline sign-off.

Next steps (today):
- Assemble initial exports and run redaction script in staging.
- Kick off internal security review (assign code owners).
- Draft cover email with short FAQ addressing the top 3 Greenline concerns.

Appendix: quick command snippets (copied from workshop demos):
- Export NSG: az network nsg show -g RG -n nsg-name --query "securityRules" > nsgrules.json
- Pull activity logs: az monitor activity-log list --resource-group RG --start-time 2025-09-23 --end-time 2025-09-30 > activity.json
- Key access test: az keyvault key show --vault-name greenline-kv --name customer-kek --query key.kid

Notes to self: keep evidence filenames consistent, include both raw and redacted versions locally for audit trail.  

End of brief.
